items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: This was before Daddy-O. See, Daddy-O was the first full-time disc jockey, but I was the first part-time disc jockey. I was on there before Daddy-O and before Anya Whip.

ctx.x: I think I've got enough of that. On that, how did you, from the Sentinel, where did you work?

Well, from the Sentinel, what I did, like I told you, radio was coming in, in the focus at the time. And I ran into a young man by the name of Richard Rising, who was a white guy who was working at WJBW, radio station here on the corner of Camp and Canal. Well, I used to listen to Richard quite often. And, well, after about, maybe about a year or so, Richard and I developed a friendship over the telephone. So he asked me, said, why don't you come down and see what I'm doing one night? And I just got in my…
Now, with the white kids from Tulane and Lowell, would they come down to the blinds, though?
